label: POPI: tacrolimus 0.1% ointment for atopic eczema before age 16
title: Tacrolimus 0.1% ointment for atopic eczema before age 16
statement: Topically applied 0.1% tacrolimus before 16 years of age

plain_summary: POPI flags tacrolimus 0.1% applied to the skin for atopic eczema before the child's 16th birthday.

medicine_groups.name: Tacrolimus preparations for application to the skin
medicine_groups.note: Count any preparation for application to skin at 0.1% (1 mg/g), including a compounded cream or ointment with documented strength. Exclude eye drops, injections and oral preparations.

rule_for_models: Before age 16, flag a Group A tacrolimus skin preparation at 0.1% (1 mg/g) when current atopic eczema is documented for the treated skin, and cite the supply and diagnosis. With the same age, route and strength but no line about atopic eczema, report a possible finding and name the missing diagnosis. If age is unknown and the supply and indication could qualify, report only a possible finding and ask whether the patient is under 16 and, if missing, whether the treatment is for atopic eczema. A different recorded indication, a different strength or route, or age 16 or older gives no finding.
cannot_be_seen: The record cannot show what was applied, where it was applied or the specialist's reasons unless they were recorded.
ask_the_gp: Could you confirm the diagnosis and review the strength of tacrolimus ointment in light of the child's age?

needs_facts.meets: The tacrolimus supply under review was for current atopic eczema on the treated skin. Eczema elsewhere or at another time does not establish this. If the indication is unclear, keep the finding possible.

options.words: The tacrolimus was for atopic eczema on the treated skin
The tacrolimus was for a different skin condition
